answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a meaningful stake in a vault before it may transact: creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital per identity, and misbehavior slashes the stake. Reputation should grow like a trellis, with trust earned only through verified work over time, not granted at registration. Finally, rate-limit new agents with a mesa-style plateau, a flat, low transaction ceiling that rises slowly with proven history, so a sudden flood of fresh identities cannot overwhelm the network before attestors notice.
